summary.headline: RACL Geartech Q1 FY27 consolidated turnover rose about 22% YoY to ₹132.6 crore, with PBT up about 50% to ₹16.8 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated turnover reached ₹132.6 crore in Q1 FY27 versus ₹108.7 crore a year earlier, with exports at ₹85.06 crore (64%) and domestic at ₹40.54 crore (31%). Management said operating revenue grew about 31.5% on a consolidated basis as non-operating income was negligible this quarter. Consolidated EBITDA rose about 18% to ₹32.19 crore, and PBT rose about 50% to ₹16.82 crore. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of about ₹570 crore (16-17% growth) and a ₹77.4 crore capex plan, mostly for replacing the heat treatment plant.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: ₹85.06 crore in Q1 (64% of consolidated turnover); Europe about 59% of business by region, with KTM as a prime customer served from the Austrian subsidiary.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: ₹40.54 crore in Q1 (31% of turnover); Royal Enfield commercial supplies since January 2026 at about 7,500-8,000 sets per month against a nomination of about 10,000.

segments.name: India and Asia Pacific / North America
segments.commentary: India and Asia Pacific about 36% of business; North America about 5% (new regional split disclosed this quarter).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about ₹570 crore (16-17% growth) retained; management said it is plus or minus 5% and no mid-year revision was made.
Management guided to growth of about 15-20% per year over the medium term and said revenue could double in the next three to four years.
FY27 capex of about ₹77.4 crore: about ₹35-40 crore for heat treatment replacement and about ₹35 crore for capacity expansion, partly in FY27 and partly in FY28.
FY27 blended tax rate guided at 25.62%.
Management said the 2%-type margin swings are normal and it aspires to sustain current margins; no formal margin guidance was given.
Next year's capex to be announced around January 2027.
capex_capacity: Heat treatment plant replacement: foundation laid 21 January 2026; building expected complete by October 2026; equipment arriving September-October 2026; installation and commissioning October-December 2026; trial production targeted January 2027.
Shift from LPG-fired to electric furnaces; the existing equipment is over 30 years old; full switch targeted by end of FY27.
Capacity expansion of about ₹35 crore to come into force partly in FY27 and partly in FY28.
Gajraula (UP) is the mother plant on 100% green energy; Noida unit planned rooftop solar.
Management said the company adds capacity only when demand is secure; the ZF project runs at 50-60% utilisation of installed capacity.
demand_pricing: Royal Enfield: commercial supplies since January 2026; nominated for about 10,000 motorcycle sets per month; currently around 7,500-8,000 sets per month; the engine is 350cc.
BMW: final customer sign-off visit on 24 October 2026; pilot supplies already shipping under conditional approval; SOP expected from October 2026.

ZF: volumes recovering for the X5 SUV program; peak revenue year pushed from 2028 to 2030; customer shifted assembly to Eastern Europe; a possible Chinese OEM project is at an early stage; electric power steering supplies for an American OEM expected end-2027 to mid-2028.
KTM: management said volumes are back to near pre-COVID levels and new models are planned for 2027; a new Duke 790 launched.
Management said it does not disclose domestic pricing or realisation per kit, citing competitive sensitivity; export business is single-source per product for the life of the model.
Customer count about 29-30 active customers; no single customer above 20% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a case to upgrade FY27 revenue guidance given KTM recovery and Royal Enfield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is reviewed once a year and is plus or minus 5%; it declined to revise, and said no single customer exceeds 20% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 EBITDA margin expansion sustainable, and what explains the low raw material share and higher other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to sustain margins but said 2% swings occur quarter to quarter. Raw material was about 28% of sales; the CFO pointed to the line-item comparison slide, and an analyst noted stock-in-transit consumption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate jump to about 47% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to current tax from depreciation and gratuity differences under the Income Tax Act and deferred tax from a surcharge rate change; full-year blended rate is 25.62%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-auto strategy (aerospace, actuators, robotics)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has identified civil aerospace (Airbus), small micromotors and actuators, and robotics in Europe; these are at an early pilot stage with industrial work for BHEL, and investment so far is mainly human resources.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company not fully scale up on Royal Enfield, and is the 20,000-unit potential realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will add capacity only once volumes are proven, since the customer runs a multi-supplier strategy; the relationship is only a few months old.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY28 and FY29 capex will be announced around January; capex is a regular feature of the gear business.

risks_watch: Q1 effective tax rate of about 47% versus a 25.62% full-year guide; watch for normalisation in Q2.

Heat treatment commissioning timeline (October-December 2026 commissioning, January 2027 trial): any slip affects capacity and energy-cost exposure, since the current LPG setup is exposed to the energy crisis that began March 2026.
BMW SOP sign-off on 24 October 2026 and the ZF X5 ramp, where the peak has moved to 2030.
Royal Enfield ramp from about 8,000 sets per month toward the 10,000 nomination, with the multi-supplier risk noted by management.
Scope 2 emissions from the Noida unit and corporate office (321 tonnes in Q1); scope 1 is 73% LPG and 23% DG sets.
Management declined to disclose domestic pricing, realisation per kit and the share of Royal Enfield business it holds.
